git-repo.ps1.objective: Review, pull, or push changes in the selected Git repository.
git-repo.ps1.requires: Git for Windows; run from an existing terminal
git-repo.ps1.notes: Standalone Git check, push and pull using the current repository or -Path. Default: -Action Check; add -Details for file names. -Action Push previews changes and requires typed approval before staging, committing and pushing. -Action Pull refuses a dirty tree and only fast-forwards. Run in a terminal; no profile dependency. File-name checks are not a secret scanner.
git-repo.ps1.launchArgs: -Path (Read-Host "Full path to the target Git repository")
git-repo.ps1.details: The launch command runs a read-only check. For reviewed publishing or updates, use -Action Push or -Action Pull in the same terminal. Push previews changes and asks for typed approval; Pull requires no local changes. Check uses the last known remote state without fetching. File-name checks do not scan file contents for secrets.

completion.next: Review errors and confirm the intended branch/remote. A Check result does not refresh remote state.

git-security.ps1.objective: Review a GitHub security-log export for unfamiliar access and activity.
git-security.ps1.requires: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later. Uses a downloaded export; does not sign in to GitHub.
git-security.ps1.notes: Run .\git-security.ps1 -Account your-github-handle. Export JSON from GitHub, then press Enter for the newest matching download. Shows actionable unreviewed access/security events. Complete reviews without flags update a local checkpoint; flagged exports require explicit acknowledgement. Changes local history only, never GitHub settings. ALL CLEAR means no rule matches, not proof of no compromise.
git-security.ps1.input: Your GitHub account name and a downloaded security-log export (JSON, JSON.GZ, or ZIP). Looks in your Downloads folder unless another path is supplied.
git-security.ps1.details: Download your security log from GitHub first. The script reviews the newest matching download or asks for a path. It saves local review history after a complete review without flags; flagged results require acknowledgement. ALL CLEAR means no matching warning rules, not proof that the account is secure.

completion.result: New security-log events matching the review rules, or a report that no warning rules matched.
completion.next: Confirm actors and changes in the original GitHub log. ALL CLEAR is not proof that the account is secure.
completion.blocked: A cancelled, failed, or unconfirmed action is not complete. Review the results before retrying.

BEC-RISK-ASSESSMENT.ps1.result: Findings and checks that could not run for the selected account. Review the evidence before deciding whether the incident is resolved.
BEC-RISK-ASSESSMENT.ps1.next: If containment is needed and approved, continue with BEC-CONTAIN-ERADICATE. Otherwise record the findings and follow your incident process.
BEC-RISK-ASSESSMENT.ps1.blocked: If a required check cannot run, resolve the missing access or data before deciding the account is clear.

BEC-CONTAIN-ERADICATE.ps1.result: Completed, failed, and skipped actions, plus any remaining investigation or unwanted access to remove.
BEC-CONTAIN-ERADICATE.ps1.next: Continue with BEC-RECOVER-VALIDATE before restoring access. Keep the account contained until cleanup is complete and recovery is approved.
BEC-CONTAIN-ERADICATE.ps1.blocked: A failed or cancelled action is not completed. Review the action results and maintain containment until the incident owner approves the next step.

BEC-RECOVER-VALIDATE.ps1.result: Recovery checks and whether the account was enabled. A pending sync is not confirmed recovery.
BEC-RECOVER-VALIDATE.ps1.next: Verify the user can sign in with MFA, record the result, and monitor for new suspicious activity for 48 hours. Unresolved issues remain open.
BEC-RECOVER-VALIDATE.ps1.blocked: If readiness or restored access cannot be verified, stop and return to the incident owner. Do not repeatedly enable the account to bypass a failed check.

preparation: BEC means business email compromise: a suspected takeover of a work email account.
Use the approved Windows support computer and an account allowed to manage the customer’s Microsoft 365 environment. Accounts linked to local Active Directory also need permission there.
Have the user’s full sign-in address (UPN) ready. Run Prepare FIELD KIT if the required modules are missing.

Extract all package files into one folder. Keep the internal handoff filenames alongside the display-named scripts. Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7 on that computer and keep that window open for the workflow.
The first sign-in requests permissions for assessment, containment and recovery. The assessment itself makes no tenant changes; change actions still require approval.
